Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
712 AM EDT Sun Oct 4 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 223 AM EDT Sunday...

No significant changes made.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 223 AM EDT Sunday...

1. A cold front will move through Monday bringing some chances 
for rain, northwesterly breezes, and a reinforcing shot of cooler 
temperatures.

2. Becoming seasonably mild through the rest of the week. A 
series of weak fronts will bring periodic chances of light rain but 
no significant events are expected.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 223 AM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Today will be a seasonable day with temperatures in most 
areas at least reaching 60 to the mid 60s. River valley fog will end 
early this evening as the combination of some building high level 
clouds and increasing southeast to south flow will develop. A 
prefrontal trough will approach later this evening. It will try to 
produce a few showers as moisture lifts north ahead of it. However, 
there's very little to work with, and so perhaps a stray shower 
north of Route 11 in our area of responsibility could occur.

The actual frontal boundary will shift east beyond midnight through 
Monday night. There remains little change with regard to the strong 
dynamical forcing that will be present, but marginal moisture 
parameters. A few post-frontal showers could take place, especially 
along the international border as the vort max associated with the 
upper trough arrives with sufficient moisture to still allow some 
activity, particularly over northwest facing slopes. The bulk of the 
cold air will not arrive until well after the rain has exited, so 
there will be limited, but not impossible, chance for a few 
flakes over our northern summits.

The air mass coming in for Monday is quite chilly. Brisk northwest 
winds of 25 to 35 mph and temperatures lingering in the 50s, except 
in the Upper Valley, will make it feel very much like Autumn. 
Minimum temperatures for Monday night range from the mid 20s to mid 
30s with some upper 30s lingering near Lake Champlain. Winds will 
keep blowing over most areas, and this should preclude fog or frost. 
The core of the coldest air will start pulling away Tuesday, but it 
will be a chilly day in the upper 40s to mid 50s and steady winds 
remaining. Heading into Tuesday night, high pressure will roll in, 
and this should allow winds to slacken and radiative cooling to take 
over. Still, ensemble guidance is relatively stayed with upper 20s 
to upper 30s, and did nudge things a couple degrees towards some 
colder solutions. There could be some fairly widespread frost 
Tuesday night into early Wednesday.

KEY MESSAGE 2: High pressure will exit east into the Atlantic. This 
will allow our temperatures to moderate. Over the course of the 
latter portion of the weak, there will be plenty of northern stream 
systems that will make their way across the mid-latitude westerlies. 
None of them are particularly strong, but may offer some reinforcing 
shots of cool air and light rain. So rather seasonable conditions 
are expected. Heading into the extended time frame by next weekend, 
a fairly broad ridge will amplify across much of the CONUS east of 
the Rockies.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 12Z Monday...Fog lingers across Vermont east of the
Greens, a strip of lake clouds extends along the western half of
Lake Champlain near KPBG, and some stratus has developed over
the Adirondacks. Given thickness of the fog over KMPV, set it to
go for at least another hour before starting to lift. Guidance
did not have a great handle on the stratus over the Adirondacks,
and so it is hard to know how long it will last, but after 14z,
generally VFR conditions are expected with passing high clouds.
South winds will increase to 9 to 14 knots sustained with gusts
18 to 25 knots possible, especially for KPBG and KBTV. After
22z, winds will slacken briefly, but begin to increase at KPBG
and KBTV again later in the night. Some light rain showers will
be possible, but with relatively little impact to visibility or
ceilings, mainly in the 05z-14z Monday time frame.

Outlook...

Monday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Monday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Thursday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
